optimize_reason: Net-margin annual improvement benchmarked against broad sector peers instead of subindustry. Broader peer sets preserve more cross-sectional dispersion in the profitability-trend signal, which raises both turnover and realized returns; economics unchanged: firms whose net margin improves year over year within their sector are repriced upward because the market underreacts to persistent margin expansion.

Two-year net-margin improvement at sector level. Longer comparison baseline filters single-quarter filing noise and fiscal-year misalignment across GLB jurisdictions, isolating durable profitability regime shifts; the 504-day window already produced the highest returns (4.52%) at subindustry, and sector grouping should lift dispersion further.

Dual-horizon confirmation: annual margin trend plus the most recent quarterly inflection. A firm whose margin is improving on both the year-over-year trend and the latest quarter shows genuine operating momentum rather than a stale base effect; the fast leg also raises turnover above the 5% floor.

Cash-generation trend (operating cash flow over revenue) benchmarked against the whole market rather than a peer group. Cash conversion is harder to manipulate than accrual earnings, so a market-relative improvement in cash margin is a cleaner signal of genuine competitive gain; the widest cross-section maximizes dispersion and turnover.
